## Claims
- [source-backed] The formal conjecture is that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal. [source-6, lines 10-16]
- [source-backed] The stronger suspected statement is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 18-21; source-6, lines 56-70]
- [source-backed] The authors report computational verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(q=n-r\le5\). [source-6, lines 46-54]
- [source-backed] A separate open question asks for minimal generating sets for general type-\(A\) ideals \(I_w\). [source-6, lines 88-102]
- [proved] For \(i=j=1\), \(a=\min(q-1,r-1)\), \(b=1\), and \(N=\binom{a+1}{a}=\min(r,q)\); the two displayed families specialize to \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_{\min(r,q)}\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_{\min(r,q)}\}\).
- [proved] If \(a=0\), equivalently \(i=q\) or \(j=r\) under \(1\le i\le q,\ 1\le j\le r\), then \(N=1\); both proposed families are the singleton \(\{s_{i^j}\}\). These are trivial minimality cases provided \(s_{i^j}\ne0\) and Theorem 5.4’s generation assertion is used.
- [proved] The smallest interior case with \(b>1\) is \((r,q,i,j)=(3,3,2,2)\), where \(a=1\), \(b=2\), \(N=3\), and the two families are \((22,32,33)\) and \((22,221,222)\).
- [computed] The prior finite certificate for \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\) gives \(N=10\), quotient \(\mathbb Z^{10}\), and basis candidates \(F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222)\); it supports the conjecture conditionally on the Pieri presentation and generation hypotheses. [artifact 0b05e147fd3b8f028a0683ee0de19704b04f214954cc0d8c387547f8371d7299]
- [computed] The attempted fresh computation timed out after 10 seconds, producing no new example, counterexample, or independent verification. [artifact a52fff03e3b77fa37fcd06e5d5f57b064ca0a2f89b10901aaa4bb057bfd6006b]
- [unsupported] No counterexample to minimality is supplied or obtained here.

## Strategy
Use \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) to separate singleton boundary cases, the uniform \(i=j=1\) family, and the first \(b>1\) interior case. Treat the artifact-backed \((5,6,2,2)\) calculation only as finite support beyond the paper’s reported range.

## Gaps
The fresh computation failed, and the prior \((5,6,2,2)\) computation lacks an independently implemented LR/Smith verification. No independent-review record was supplied for this attempt.

## Next
Produce an independent exact LR/Smith certificate for \((3,3,2,2)\) or \((5,6,2,2)\), including a unimodular minor and integral reduction of all relation rows.
